misconceptions.description: Leaving weight off the free body diagram
misconceptions.trigger: learner draws support or tension forces but omits gravity on a massive object
misconceptions.feedback: Any object with mass has weight. If the body is isolated, weight must appear on the free body diagram unless the problem explicitly neglects it.

misconceptions.description: Drawing tension toward the object instead of away along the cable
misconceptions.trigger: learner points cable tension into the body
misconceptions.feedback: An ideal cable can only pull, not push. Tension on the isolated body acts along the cable and away from the body.

misconceptions.description: Adding internal forces that should not appear on the isolated body
misconceptions.trigger: learner includes forces from parts that are inside the chosen system boundary
misconceptions.feedback: A free body diagram should show only external forces acting on the isolated body or subsystem.
